chapter: Early influences, Oliver date and trombone peers
title: Trummy Young and the Denmark record
summary: Trummy Young copies him note for note; in Denmark a patron played him a record of I'm Confessing.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: You influenced like most of the trombone players since your time, I mean you've been like one of the major influences in jazz, I said and you have influenced so many young trombone players, I mean trombone players since your playing. What are some of the trombone players that you've listened to that you also we impressed by their playing ... or even younger ones.

I'd be glad to say it, Trummy Young. Note for note. He came and told me, he said, "I'm going to steal every thing that I can from you." And I said, "Thank you." It made me work harder. I have a record I made back there over in Denmark and the guy, I have his picture there, he sent for me. He owned a chocolate factory over there and he was a very nice guy. So, the first night I got there, got off the plane and ate dinner and he walked downstairs and said he wanted me to listen to a record. He played "I'm Confessing." (that phrases) I said it I know it's the same notes but then (I played) it a lot, you know.
Trummy played but well, I thought it was me plenty of times. And I mean it made me feel good. ( ... ) Makes me try to do better.
